text: Why can no lossless compressor shrink every input?
choices: Because the compressor's own header occupies space that cannot be recovered.
Because compression is only defined for inputs above a minimum length.
There are 2ⁿ inputs of length n but only 2ⁿ - 1 strings shorter than n, so two inputs must collide and the decompressor cannot tell them apart.
Because random data has maximum entropy, and most inputs are random.
explanation: Three lines, using Chapter 17's sum of powers of two. The conclusion is stronger than "some inputs do not shrink": for every lossless compressor, some inputs must *grow*. Verified — 200 of 200 random 64-byte inputs grew. Which is why every real compressor stores an incompressible block uncompressed with a flag saying so; that flag is the unavoidable growth, minimized.
